title: Implement paths.ts: Kiro-home resolution + containment assertion
description:
## Objective
Resolve the Kiro home dir and per-type target dirs, with a test seam and a safety assertion that prevents writes outside ~/.kiro and under ~/.kiro/skills/.

## Context
All file writes route through these resolved paths. The containment assertion structurally enforces the PRD boundary (never touch skills/, never escape ~/.kiro). The KIRO_HOME env seam lets tests run isolated.

## Scope
In scope:
- kiroHome(): process.env.KIRO_HOME if set, else path.join(os.homedir(), ".kiro")
- targetDir(type) for "agents" | "prompts" | "steering"
- lockfilePath() = <home>/.kiro-blackbytes.json
- assertInsideKiroHome(target): throws if resolved path escapes home OR is under <home>/skills/
Out of scope:
- actual file writing (installer)

## Components Touched
- src/core/paths.ts (new)

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- Project scaffold must exist

## Assumptions / Constraints
- KIRO_HOME env override is the test seam (design §9). Production default ~/.kiro.
- Use path.resolve + prefix check for containment; reject ".." escapes.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Unit-tested (covered in the units task): KIRO_HOME honored, fallback to ~/.kiro, targetDir correct, lockfilePath correct
- assertInsideKiroHome throws for ".." escape and for skills/ paths, passes for normal targets
- biome + tsc clean
acceptance_criteria:
- kiroHome() honors KIRO_HOME env, else falls back to ~/.kiro
- targetDir("agents"|"prompts"|"steering") returns correct absolute paths
- lockfilePath() = <home>/.kiro-blackbytes.json
- assertInsideKiroHome throws for ".." escape AND for any path under <home>/skills/; passes for normal targets
- tsc + biome clean (self-verify with a quick scratch script if unit task not yet done)

title: Implement lockfile.ts: read, validate, atomic write
description:
## Objective
Read/validate/write the ownership lockfile ~/.kiro/.kiro-blackbytes.json (schema 1). Missing file => empty ownership. Invalid JSON or unknown schema => clear error. Write atomically (temp + rename).

## Context
The lockfile is the record of which files the tool owns; only owned files may be overwritten on update. Atomic write guards against corruption on interruption.

## Scope
In scope:
- read(): absent => empty-ownership result; valid => {schema, version, updatedAt, files[]}; malformed/bad-schema => throw descriptive error
- write({version, files}): sets schema:1 + fresh ISO updatedAt, writes <path>.tmp then rename
- files stored with forward-slash separators
Out of scope:
- deciding what goes in files[] (installer computes that)

## Components Touched
- src/core/lockfile.ts (new); uses paths.ts lockfilePath()

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- paths.ts (for lockfilePath); scaffold

## Assumptions / Constraints
- schema === 1 only; reject others rather than guessing ownership (REQ-007).
- Atomic = write temp in same dir + fs.rename (same-filesystem atomicity).

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Unit-tested: missing=>empty, valid parse, malformed/bad-schema throw, write round-trips through read
- biome + tsc clean
acceptance_criteria:
- read() on missing file => empty ownership ({files:[]})
- read() parses valid lockfile into {schema, version, updatedAt, files[]}
- read() throws descriptive error on malformed JSON or schema !== 1
- write({version,files}) sets schema:1 + fresh ISO updatedAt, writes <path>.tmp then rename, round-trips through read()
- files stored with forward-slash separators
- tsc + biome clean
close_reason: Implemented src/core/lockfile.ts: read (missing=>empty, malformed/bad-schema throw), write (schema:1+ISO updatedAt, atomic tmp+rename, forward-slash sorted files). Self-check passed; tsc+biome clean.

title: Implement bundle.ts: enumerate bundle into BundleFile[]
description:
## Objective
Walk the shipped bundle/ directory and produce a typed BundleFile[] describing every file to install and its target under ~/.kiro/.

## Context
The directory tree IS the manifest (design decision D2 — no bundle.json). The installer and list command both consume this enumeration.

## Scope
In scope:
- agents/: *.json + *.md (flat)
- prompts/: *.md (flat)
- steering/: **/*.md (recursive, preserve relative subpath)
- ignore other extensions and stray files at bundle/ root
- BundleFile = { type: "agents"|"prompts"|"steering", relPath, absSource, target } where relPath is relative to the type target dir; target resolved via paths.targetDir(type)
- expose a way to derive the lockfile-style rel path (e.g. "agents/bb.json")
Out of scope:
- reading/comparing target files (installer)

## Components Touched
- src/core/bundle.ts (new); uses paths.ts

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- paths.ts (targetDir); scaffold

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Bundle path must be anchored to the PACKAGE ROOT (resolved from the compiled module location, e.g. import.meta.url), NOT process.cwd() — so it resolves correctly when run via npx from any directory.
- Steering nesting must be preserved in both relPath and target.

## Risks / Gotchas
- npx runs from arbitrary cwd; resolving bundle/ relative to cwd will find nothing. Anchor to module location.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Unit-tested with a fixture bundle: one entry per matching file across 3 subdirs; steering nesting preserved; non-md/json ignored
- Resolves whether run from dist/ or via npx
- biome + tsc clean
acceptance_criteria:
- one BundleFile per matching file across agents/ (json+md), prompts/ (md), steering/ (**/*.md)
- steering nesting preserved in relPath AND target
- non-md/json files and stray bundle/ root files ignored
- bundle path anchored to package root (import.meta.url), resolves under npx from any cwd
- lockfile-style rel path (e.g. agents/bb.json) derivable
- tsc + biome clean
close_reason: Implemented src/core/bundle.ts: enumerate() walks agents(json,md)/prompts(md)/steering(**/*.md), ignores other ext; BundleFile{type,relPath,absSource,target}; bundleRoot anchored via import.meta.url (pkg root, not cwd); steering nesting preserved; lockKey helper. Self-check 5 entries OK; tsc+biome clean.

title: Implement installer.ts: write + sync primitive
description:
## Objective
Implement the core sync(mode) algorithm and low-level write(file). sync enumerates the bundle, compares against disk + prior lockfile, classifies each file, leaves orphans in place, and writes the lockfile only after all copies succeed.

## Context
This is the heart of the tool — init and update are thin wrappers over sync. Correctness of ownership tracking and override semantics lives here (REQ-001/002/004/006/007).

## Scope
In scope:
- write(file): assertInsideKiroHome(target) -> mkdir -p dirname -> copy source to target (overwrite)
- sync(mode): for each bundle file classify ADDED (target absent) / OVERWRITTEN (init over a pre-existing non-owned file) / UPDATED (owned, content differs) / UNCHANGED (content equal); compute ORPHANED (in prior lockfile, not in bundle) and LEAVE on disk; then lockfile.write({version: pkgVersion, files: allBundleRelPaths})
- contentDiffers(file): byte comparison of source vs target
- lockfile written ONLY after all file copies succeed; copy error aborts before lockfile write
- return the list of (file, outcome)
Out of scope:
- stdout formatting (commands do that)

## Components Touched
- src/core/installer.ts (new); uses paths.ts, lockfile.ts, bundle.ts

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- paths.ts, lockfile.ts, bundle.ts must all exist (sync uses all three)

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Override-on-write is the chosen policy: bundled files overwrite local edits; user-authored files NOT in the bundle are never touched.
- Orphans are reported, never deleted (Q-001).
- pkgVersion read from package.json version.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Must not write the lockfile if a copy fails (would overstate disk state).
- Idempotency: two runs must converge to identical disk + lockfile.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Fully covered by the sync tests task: empty home=>all ADDED; re-run=>all UNCHANGED; user-authored non-bundle file untouched; hand-edited owned file=>UPDATED restored; removed-from-bundle=>ORPHANED still on disk; copy failure=>lockfile not written
- biome + tsc clean
acceptance_criteria:
- empty home => all ADDED + lockfile lists all; re-run => all UNCHANGED
- user-authored file NOT in bundle never touched/listed
- hand-edited owned file => UPDATED, content restored
- bundle file removed => ORPHANED, left on disk (not deleted)
- copy failure aborts BEFORE lockfile write
- two runs converge (idempotent); contentDiffers = byte comparison
- tsc + biome clean
close_reason: Implemented src/core/installer.ts: write() (assertInsideKiroHome+mkdir+copy), sync() classifies ADDED/OVERWRITTEN/UPDATED/UNCHANGED/ORPHANED, copies all before atomic lockfile.write (aborts pre-lockfile on failure), contentDiffers=byte compare, packageVersion(). Added KIRO_BLACKBYTES_BUNDLE env seam to bundle.bundleRoot for tests. Self-check all 6 outcomes OK; tsc+biome clean.

title: Implement init and update commands
description:
## Objective
Thin command wrappers over sync(): init prints a fresh-install summary; update prints a diff summary (added/updated/unchanged + orphaned). Both exit 0 on success.

## Context
init is the default command (npx kiro-blackbytes). update re-syncs to the current bundle version. Both call the same sync primitive; they differ only in reporting.

## Scope
In scope:
- commands/init.ts: run sync, print counts of added/overwritten grouped by type (agents/prompts/steering)
- commands/update.ts: run sync, print added/updated/unchanged + list orphaned
- plain text to stdout; return success (exit 0)
Out of scope:
- arg parsing/dispatch (cli.ts task)
- the sync algorithm itself (installer task)

## Components Touched
- src/commands/init.ts (new), src/commands/update.ts (new); use installer.sync

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- installer.ts (sync) must exist

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Override is silent (no prompts) — non-interactive v1.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Behavior exercised by the integration test: init on empty home reports N added; update after a bundle change reports updated/added + unchanged + orphans
- biome + tsc clean
acceptance_criteria:
- init on empty home reports N added grouped by type (agents/prompts/steering), exit 0
- update after a bundle change reports added/updated/unchanged + lists orphaned, exit 0
- plain text to stdout; non-interactive (no prompts)
- tsc + biome clean
close_reason: Implemented src/commands/init.ts + update.ts (+ shared report.ts tally/keysOf). init=sync(init)+added/overwritten/unchanged summary; update=sync(update)+added/updated/overwritten/unchanged + orphaned list. Both exit 0. Self-check OK; tsc+biome clean.

title: Implement list command with install-status computation
description:
## Objective
Compute and print per-item install status by joining bundle x disk x lockfile, grouped by type, plus the bundle (package) version. Exit 0.

## Context
list lets the user inspect what the bundle contains and whether each item is installed/modified/orphaned before running init/update. Surfaces "modified" so the user knows update would revert a local edit.

## Scope
In scope:
- statuses per item: installed (in lockfile + present) / not installed (in bundle, target missing) / modified (in lockfile, byte-differs from bundle) / orphaned (in lockfile, not in bundle)
- group output by type; show bundle version from package.json
- exit 0
Out of scope:
- mutating any files

## Components Touched
- src/commands/list.ts (new); uses lockfile.ts + bundle.ts (+ byte compare)

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- lockfile.ts and bundle.ts must exist (status needs both)

## Assumptions / Constraints
- modified detected via byte comparison (DQ-003: files are few/small, byte compare acceptable).

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Covered by integration test: each item printed with correct marker; modified detected; orphans listed; version shown; exit 0
- biome + tsc clean
acceptance_criteria:
- each bundle item printed with correct status: installed / not installed / modified / orphaned
- modified detected via byte comparison
- orphaned (lockfile-only) items listed
- bundle version shown (from package.json)
- exit 0; tsc + biome clean
close_reason: Implemented src/commands/list.ts: joins bundle x disk x lockfile; per-item status installed/not installed/modified/orphaned via byte compare + ownership; grouped by type; orphans (owned, not in bundle) listed; shows version; exit 0. All 4 statuses self-checked; tsc+biome clean.

title: Implement cli.ts arg dispatch, help, and exit codes

## Scope

- success => exit 0
Out of scope:
- the command implementations themselves

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- init/update commands and list command must exist

## Assumptions / Constraints

- Plain text stdout for success, stderr for errors.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Covered by integration test: no-arg and init both run init; update/list route; --help prints usage exit 0; unknown command => usage on stderr + non-zero; thrown error => stderr message + non-zero
- biome + tsc clean
acceptance_criteria:

- update/list route correctly
- --help/-h prints usage to stdout, exit 0
- unknown command => usage to stderr, non-zero exit
- thrown command error => message to stderr + non-zero exit (no raw stack as primary output)

close_reason: Implemented src/cli.ts dispatch: argv[2] default init; routes init/update/list; --help/-h + --version/-v; unknown=>usage to stderr exit 1; try/catch wraps run, thrown errors=>stderr message exit 1; success exit 0. title: Ship bundle/ in npm tarball and add pack smoke test
description:
## Objective
Ensure bundle/ and dist/ are included in the published package and resolved at runtime; verify via npm pack that the tarball contains them and the packed CLI installs correctly.

## Context
If bundle/ is omitted from the tarball, npx install does nothing. This task guarantees the published artifact is complete and buildable from a fresh clone.

## Scope
In scope:
- package.json "files" includes dist and bundle (all three subdirs)
- prepack/prepublishOnly script builds dist/ so a fresh clone publishes correctly
- npm pack smoke test: tarball contains dist/ + bundle/; installing the packed tarball and running `kiro-blackbytes init` with KIRO_HOME=<temp> installs all bundle files
Out of scope:
- actual npm publish (PQ-002, deferred)

## Components Touched
- package.json (files, prepack/prepublishOnly)

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- bin wiring (build output) must exist
- bundle content must exist (so the tarball has something to ship)

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Bundle resolution anchored to package root (see bundle.ts) so packed install works from temp KIRO_HOME.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- npm pack tarball contains dist/ and bundle/ (all 3 subdirs)
- packed tarball install + init with KIRO_HOME=temp installs all bundle files there
- dist built before pack
acceptance_criteria:
- npm pack tarball contains dist/ AND bundle/ (all 3 subdirs)
- prepack/prepublishOnly builds dist/ before pack
- installing packed tarball + running `kiro-blackbytes init` with KIRO_HOME=<temp> installs all bundle files there
close_reason: package.json files=[dist,bundle], prepack+prepublishOnly=npm run build. npm pack tarball verified: 12 bundle files + 10 dist files. Full smoke test: packed tarball installed into temp prefix, npx kiro-blackbytes init against temp KIRO_HOME installed all 12 files + lockfile (bundle resolved from installed location via import.meta.url anchoring).
